page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.medium is an entry-level virtual server instance belonging to the Shared instance family. Running on the KVM hypervisor with the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance allocates two virtual CPUs backed by a single physical execution core with two threads. It provides 8.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. Architectural instruction support includes AVX and AVX-512F vector extensions, as well as AES cryptographic instructions, with access to 35 MB of shared L3 cache.

Benchmark results reflect the constrained throughput inherent to a two-vCPU entry-tier footprint. CPU testing demonstrates modest computational capability, registering 1107.09 in single-core stress-ng tests and a composite PassMark CPU score of 2641.62. Memory throughput metrics show uncached large-block read speeds of 16.61 GB/sec and write speeds of 14.38 GB/sec. Application testing reveals baseline throughput, with Redis recording 2.49 million SET operations per second and static web serving achieving 1.69 GB/sec.

The instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated graphics hardware, requiring external block storage for persistent data. From a resource perspective, it offers an economical deployment model for lower-intensity tasks where peak execution speed is not critical. The hardware profile is best configured for development environments, low-traffic web applications, lightweight background jobs, microservices, and secondary staging workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.medium is a general-purpose virtual machine within the Shared instance family. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz, delivering two vCPUs across one physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The system includes 8.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It lacks dedicated GPUs and includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes. Synthetic benchmarks place its compute and memory throughput in the lower percentiles, with a PassMark CPU score of 2641.62 and memory write bandwidth of 14.38 GB/sec. Due to its limited processing capacity and entry-level hardware density, this instance is suited for lightweight web serving, staging servers, basic testing environments, and non-critical background services.
